original_query: select c_name, c_custkey, o_orderkey, o_orderdate, o_totalprice, sum(l_quantity) from customer, orders, lineitem where o_orderkey in ( select l_orderkey from lineitem group by l_orderkey having sum(l_quantity) > 313 ) and c_custkey = o_custkey and o_orderkey = l_orderkey group by c_name, c_custkey, o_orderkey, o_orderdate, o_totalprice order by o_totalprice desc, o_orderdate limit 100;
rewritten_query:
WITH order_qty AS (
    SELECT l_orderkey,
           SUM(l_quantity) AS sum_l_quantity
    FROM lineitem
    GROUP BY l_orderkey
    HAVING SUM(l_quantity) > 313
)
SELECT c.c_name,
       c.c_custkey,
       o.o_orderkey,
       o.o_orderdate,
       o.o_totalprice,
       oq.sum_l_quantity
FROM customer c
JOIN orders o
  ON o.o_custkey = c.c_custkey
JOIN order_qty oq
  ON oq.l_orderkey = o.o_orderkey
ORDER BY o.o_totalprice DESC, o.o_orderdate
LIMIT 100;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Replace the IN subquery plus the second lineitem join with a single pre-aggregated derived table/CTE (order_qty) computing SUM(l_quantity) per l_orderkey with HAVING SUM(l_quantity) > 313. Since the outer SUM(l_quantity) over the same grouping key equals the aggregate already computed, the second scan of lineitem (60M rows) is eliminated entirely.

Remove the outer GROUP BY. Because order_qty yields exactly one row per qualifying order and c_custkey/o_orderkey are unique keys, the outer aggregation is redundant; the pre-computed sum_l_quantity can be projected directly, avoiding a large GroupAggregate/Sort.

Convert old-style comma joins to explicit ANSI JOINs, making the join order (order_qty -> orders -> customer) explicit and readable. Joining the filtered aggregated result to orders/customer last leverages PK lookups on o_orderkey and c_custkey.
